sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the Home Base screen
sections.what: Loads the icons, the shared store, small UI building blocks and the child widgets this screen is made from. No visible output from this part.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond supplying every widget shown on the screen.

sections.name: NASAMissionControlView (part 1)
sections.title: Header, urgency score and orbit visuals
sections.what: Shows the Home Base title, the user's name, a momentum percentage and an urgency number out of 100. The urgency number adds 30 for each urgent open task and 20 for each pending assignment, capped at 100. Below the header it shows a mascot, a solar-system life map on wide screens and a list version on phones.
sections.why: Likely reason: a quick summary at the top, with separate layouts so the map fits both small and large screens.
sections.watch_out: The urgency weights are simple fixed numbers chosen in this file, not a measured or validated result.

sections.name: NASAMissionControlView (part 2)
sections.title: Score, benchmark, deadlines and interviews
sections.what: Shows the life score, the weekly benchmark, up to three pending assignments with their due dates, and a count of interviews. Empty lists show a short italic message instead of blank space.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The interview list only counts status 'interview', while the life map counts 'interviewing' and 'applied', so the two screens can show different numbers.

sections.name: NASAMissionControlView (part 3)
sections.title: Deadline risk, today's tasks and focus
sections.what: Shows the deadline risk widget, up to four tasks marked today or doing with a link to all tasks, a focus card with a 50 minute start button, and the project health section.
sections.why: Likely reason: puts the most actionable items, tasks and the focus button, near the bottom where the user can act on them.
sections.watch_out: The focus button starts a timer labelled 'Home Base Focus Sprint'; the timer itself was not reviewed here.

summary: The full Home Base screen: a header with urgency and momentum numbers, a life map, score and deadline cards, interviews, today's tasks, a focus start button and project health.
purpose: Gives the user one page that shows what needs attention now and what to do next.
why: Likely reason: collects the most useful summaries in one place, with separate layouts for phones and wide screens.
how: The component reads profile, tasks, assignments and internships from the store. It filters them into urgent tasks, today's tasks, pending assignments and interviews. It works out an urgency score, then draws each section from these lists. Child widgets draw the life map, score, deadlines and project health.
inputs: Store data: profile, tasks, assignments, internships and the actions for starting focus, changing tab and opening the AI assistant. No props.
outputs: The full dashboard screen. Pressing the focus button starts a 50 minute timer. Links switch to the tasks tab.
risks: Interviews are filtered on the status 'interview' while the life map uses 'interviewing' and 'applied', so the two can disagree. Several imports are never used in this file. Due dates are shown as raw stored text.
debug: If a count looks wrong, check the status values in the stored data against the names used in the filters. If a section is empty, check that the matching list is filled in the store. If the focus button does nothing, check startFocusTimer in the store.
